extracted.intended_audience: grant reviewers and molecular/virology researchers (PIs, postdocs, lab scientists preparing/examining mechanistic virology grants)
extracted.subtask_description: A research strategy section of a grant proposing mechanistic cell biology/virology experiments to define how host mismatch repair proteins and viral DNA replication activate the DNA damage response (DDR) during BKPyV infection. Contains aims, experimental designs, expected outcomes, controls, and potential problems/alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of DDR activation markers
rubrics_metrics.description: Which molecular markers indicate ATR- and ATM-dependent DDR activation and how to interpret them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ATR activation is monitored by Chk1-pS317 (Chk1 phosphorylation) and is triggered primarily by ssDNA/replication stress; ATM activation is monitored by ATM-pS1981 (ATM auto-phosphorylation) and is primarily responsive to double-strand breaks (DSBs). γH2AX (phosphorylated H2AX) marks sites of DSBs and recruits DNA repair proteins. Chk2 is mainly phosphorylated by ATM. Use these markers (immunoblotting or IF) to assess DDR pathway engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functional requirement of ATR and ATM for productive BKPyV infection
rubrics_metrics.description: Test whether ATR and ATM activity are required for viral DNA replication and production of infectious progeny.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use siRNA knockdown (single and double) of ATR and ATM in infected RPTE cells. Measure cell-associated viral DNA by real-time PCR and infectious viral titer by fluorescence IU assay. Note: real-time PCR reports quantity of primer-recognized DNA but not whether DNAs are intact/genome-length; complement with assays that assess DNA integrity (Southern blot).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess viral DNA integrity with Southern blotting
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether inhibition of DDR leads to accumulation of aberrant viral DNA replication products (e.g., dimers, concatemers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Isolate total DNA from infected cells (with/without DDR knockdown) and perform one-dimensional Southern blot with a viral-specific probe. An accumulation of higher molecular weight dimeric/concatemeric products indicates replication fork collapse or unidirectional replication due to failed fork stabilization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of micronuclei and metaphase spreads as host genome instability readouts
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate host DNA damage/genomic instability in the context of infection and DDR perturbation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantify TAg-positive micronuclei formation by IF (DAPI/TAg staining) as markers of genotoxic stress and missegregated chromosomes. Perform metaphase spreads to visualize direct damage (e.g., 'shattered metaphase' phenotype) and quantify proportion of damaged metaphases. These phenotypes should be compared between mock and infected cells and across knockdown conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative proteomic identification of host factors (SILAC + 2D LC-MS/MS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use quantitative nuclear proteomics to identify host nuclear proteins upregulated by BKPyV infection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Label RPTE cells with light/heavy amino acids (SILAC), infect one population, isolate nuclear fractions, mix, and perform 2D LC-MS/MS. Use peak intensity ratios of isotopically distinct peptides for quantitation. Validate proteomic hits (e.g., MSH6, MSH2) by Western blot and orthogonal approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functional testing of MMR (hMutSα) in viral replication and DDR activation via siRNA knockdown
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess the role of MSH6 and MSH2 (hMutSα complex) in BKPyV replication, infectious particle production, and DDR activation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transfect RPTE cells with siRNAs targeting MSH6 or MSH2 then infect with BKPyV. Readouts: Western blot for viral proteins and DDR markers, qPCR for viral DNA levels, infectious titer assays for progeny, and IF/metaphase spreads for micronuclei/host DNA damage. Expect that knockdown may not change viral protein levels or DNA quantity but can reduce infectivity and DDR marker levels (e.g., decreased Chk1-pS317).

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish viral protein (TAg) effects from viral DNA replication effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether TAg expression alone is sufficient for DDR activation or whether replicating viral DNA is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare cells transduced with TAg-expressing lentivirus to BKPyV-infected cells with similar TAg levels. Use a helicase-dead TAg mutant virus (D501A) that cannot replicate viral DNA but retains other functions to test necessity of replication. Measure Chk1-pS317 and ATM-pS1981 to assess DDR activation. Interpretation: minimal ATR activation with TAg alone and loss of DDR activation with replication-deficient virus implies viral DNA replication is the major trigger.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental suite for Aim 1.1 to test MMR role (three core assays)
rubrics_metrics.description: A defined set of assays to evaluate whether MMR proteins are required for viral replication integrity and host genome stability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform (i) Southern blot (one-dimensional) of total DNA to detect aberrant viral DNA accumulation; (ii) metaphase spreads to quantify host DNA breaks/shattered metaphases; (iii) cell cycle analysis (propidium iodide staining + flow cytometry) to measure G2/M arrest or >G2 polyploid populations. Include single and combinatorial knockdowns (MSH6, MSH2, ATR, ATM) and appropriate positive/negative controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-resolution analysis of replication intermediates (2D agarose gel electrophoresis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Resolve and identify viral replication intermediates to distinguish unidirectional replication, stalled forks, and collapsed forks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use two-dimensional agarose gel electrophoresis followed by Southern blotting on restriction-digested viral DNA: first dimension separates by mass, second by topology. Compare patterns across knockdowns (ATR/ATM/MMR) and use infected ATR/ATM knockdown cells as positive controls for replication defects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of genetic rescue to confirm specificity of siRNA phenotypes
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate that observed phenotypes from MMR knockdowns are specifically due to loss of the targeted protein.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduce siRNA-resistant MSH6 or MSH2 via lentivirus into RPTE cells and determine whether expression rescues defects in viral production and host genome stability. Use this to rule out off-target siRNA effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish mismatch repair-dependent versus -independent functions of hMutSα
rubrics_metrics.description: Test whether hMutSα's role in DDR activation depends on canonical mismatch repair machinery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Knockdown hMutLα components (MLH1, PMS2) and assess effects on DDR activation, viral titer, and genome instability. If MLH1/PMS2 knockdown does not phenocopy MSH6/MSH2 knockdown, infer that MMR-mediated DDR activation may be independent of mismatch repair endonuclease activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct-recruitment vs indirect (ssDNA) models for hMutSα-mediated DDR activation
rubrics_metrics.description: Two mechanistic models: (a) hMutSα directly recruits ATR/ATM to sites of viral replication; (b) MMR activity generates ssDNA (via EXO1) that indirectly activates ATR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test direct model with co-immunoprecipitation (co-IP) to detect TAg–hMutSα–ATR/ATM interactions and ChIP to detect ATR/ATM association with viral DNA (compare with MSH6/MSH2 knockdowns). Test indirect model by knocking down EXO1 or MLH1 and assessing DDR activation and DDR protein association with viral DNA. Reciprocal co-IPs and use of crosslinkers or nuclear isolation may help capture weak/transient interactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Co-IP and ChIP experimental design and controls
rubrics_metrics.description: Approaches to detect protein–protein and protein–DNA associations and recommended controls.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use monoclonal antibodies (e.g., pAb416 for TAg) for IP; include isotype-matched IgG and mock-infected cells as negative controls. Perform reciprocal co-IPs (pull-down ATR/ATM/MSH6/MSH2). For ChIP, immunoprecipitate ATR/ATM/γH2AX and quantify viral DNA by real-time PCR; include positive controls (DNA-damaging reagents like doxorubicin and known host damage loci). Use nuclear isolation and mild lysis conditions and consider crosslinkers (NHS-esters) if interactions are weak.

rubrics_metrics.name: Testing sufficiency of viral DNA replication to activate DDR (Aim 2.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assay whether the combination of TAg and a replicatable viral origin is sufficient to elicit DDR activation in the absence of infection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transfect a plasmid bearing the BKPyV non-coding control region (origin) or a control plasmid into RPTE cells transduced with TAg lentivirus. Identify origin-containing cells by FISH (or fluorescent protein marker) and use single-cell immunofluorescence (Chk1-pS317) to quantify DDR activation due to low transfection efficiency. Include mutant TAg (D501A helicase-dead, origin-binding mutants) and origin-mutant plasmids to confirm replication dependence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detect viral ssDNA lesions and DSBs on viral genomes (Aim 2.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct assays to detect lesions on viral DNA that could trigger ATR (ssDNA) or ATM (DSBs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (i) Use non-denaturing FISH with a nick-translated viral probe to detect viral ssDNA at single-cell level and quantify signal intensity. (ii) Use γH2AX ChIP followed by qPCR across viral genome regions to detect DSB-associated γH2AX occupancy; include positive controls and HU treatment to enrich replication stress. (iii) Use ligation-mediated PCR on low molecular weight DNA to map DSBs directly. As alternatives, perform non-denaturing Southern if single-cell sensitivity is insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perturbation/chemical treatments to modulate replication stress and probe mechanism
rubrics_metrics.description: Use chemical treatments to increase or decrease replication stress and observe effects on viral DNA lesions and DDR activation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat infected cells with hydroxyurea (HU) to induce replication stress or supplement nucleotides to reduce stress. Use aphidicolin (DNA polymerase α inhibitor) to uncouple helicase and polymerase and enrich ssDNA/DSB signals. Compare DSB formation (γH2AX ChIP) in ATR knockdown cells to infer whether DSBs arise from fork collapse in absence of ATR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use appropriate positive and negative experimental controls
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure each assay includes controls to validate specificity and interpretability of results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: ATR/ATM knockdown infected cells as positive controls for viral replication defects; isotype IgG and mock-infected cells as negative controls in IP/ChIP; doxorubicin-treated cells and known damaged host loci as positive ChIP controls; HEK-293TT complementation to propagate replication-deficient mutant virus; include single vs combinatorial knockdowns to dissect individual contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipate technical limitations and provide alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify likely experimental pitfalls and alternative approaches to obtain interpretable data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared for low transfection efficiency (use FISH or fluorescent plasmid markers), weak/transient protein interactions (use nuclear isolation, crosslinkers, mild lysis), low single-cell detection sensitivity (switch to non-denaturing Southern), and ambiguous γH2AX spread from break sites (use ligation-mediated PCR to map DSBs). Also consider alternate hypotheses (assembly defects, damaged packaged DNA) and assays (CsCl gradient, EM, viral DNA/infectious unit ratio) to test them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expected outcome logic to evaluate hypotheses
rubrics_metrics.description: Predicted experimental outcomes that would support or refute mechanistic models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: accumulation of high molecular weight viral DNA products and shattered metaphases in MMR knockdown or DDR-deficient cells supports role in replication fork integrity; decreased Chk1-pS317 with MSH6 knockdown supports hMutSα contribution to ATR activation; co-IP and ChIP showing TAg–hMutSα–ATR interactions and reduced ATR association with viral DNA upon MSH6 knockdown support direct recruitment model; lack of rescue by hMutLα knockdown suggests mismatch repair-independent role.
